Definition: from G4862 and G2553; to suffer hardship in company with:--be partaker of afflictions.
BiblicalUsage: Paul tells Timothy not to be ashamed of the testimony of the Lord nor of him His prisoner, but to be a partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God, and to endure hardness as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. Affliction is not an accident of the gospel but a share in it, and the sharing is the proof of belonging.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that affliction for the gospel is a share in it, not a shame, and I hold that enduring hardness is what good soldiers do.
